page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine features 32 vCPUs backed by 16 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz with two threads per core. Hardware specifications include 64.0 GB of dedicated system memory, providing a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. It operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps, includes zero bundled public IPv4 addresses, and contains no attached local SSD or HDD storage.

Synthetic benchmark results place the multi-core processing capability of this instance in the middle tier. The server achieves a multi-core stress-ng CPU score of 27992.16 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 10181.0. In software compilation tests using Clang, it yields a score of 21474.0, while bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reaches 127.99 GB/sec. However, single-core throughput represents a performance trade-off, reflected in a single-core stress-ng score of 1312.39 and single-threaded gzip compression of 22.88 GB/sec, both placing in the lower quarter of tested instances. Memory bandwidth metrics record 109.69 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.96 GB/sec for uncached writes.

With its high core density relative to memory capacity, the instance offers practical cost efficiency for compute-intensive tasks that do not demand extensive local storage or high RAM ratios. Operational throughput remains consistent across parallelized application execution, evidenced by Redis SET throughput reaching 26.78 million operations per second and static web serving achieving 20.38 GB/sec. The hardware configuration makes the instance suitable for multi-threaded batch operations, code compilation pipelines, web server clusters, and general high-concurrency background services.
